candidates.attacker_control: The attacker supplies the 's' session-UUID parameter (and, for upload, 'name', 'ext', 'size' plus the raw request body; for download, the FileDescriptor 'f' UUID) to the publicly mapped jpawebapi dispatcher (/dispatch/api/* or /api/*). All inputs are fully attacker-controlled HTTP parameters.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The endpoints do run under the resolved user security context (AppContext.setSecurityContext(new SecurityContext(userSession))) and DataService still applies entity-operation and row-level checks, so a holder of an arbitrary session cannot read file records the session cannot load; session UUIDs are high-entropy bearer tokens, so possession of a session ID is itself a precondition (this softens exploitability for third-party attackers); the file endpoints are plausibly intended for session-scoped client file transfer, and no comment or configuration states that jpawebapi.api.enabled must apply to them; no runtime configuration (roles granting/denying the permission) is present in the snapshot to prove a concrete victim role.
candidates.impact: A user denied the add-on's REST API permission still obtains REST-side file read/write capability: reading content of any FileDescriptor the session can load and storing arbitrary files plus creating FileDescriptor records under the session. Where the session belongs to a low-privileged or shared (e.g. anonymous, if a readable FileDescriptor is known) session, this widens access beyond the intended 'REST API enabled' boundary. The impact is bounded by middleware entity-permission and row-level checks applied to the same session, so this is an authorization bypass of the add-on's own gate rather than unrestricted data access.
candidates.prerequisites: The dispatcher mapping must be installed (jpawebapi.mapping.url is /dispatch/api/* for the web module and /api/* for the portal module, app-component.xml lines 40/56) and the attacker must possess some valid CUBA user session UUID that the middleware recognizes - e.g. the attacker's own web-portal/web-client session, a session of a user whose role explicitly denies jpawebapi.api.enabled, or a predictable/shared session such as the fixed cuba.anonymousSessionId shipped in the sample properties (modules/core/.../app.properties line 25, modules/web/.../web-app.properties line 25). Spring Security in jpawebapi-dispatcher-spring.xml permits all URLs (access=permitAll, lines 35-39), so no secondary control blocks the endpoints.
candidates.root_cause: FileUploadController.getSession (lines 168-184) and RestFileDownloadController.getSession (lines 193-209) authenticate solely by converting the 's' request parameter to a UUID and calling userSessionService.getUserSession(sessionId); they never call Authentication.begin(), so the specific-permission check 'session.isSpecificPermitted("jpawebapi.api.enabled")' defined by the add-on (Authentication.java:55, 91-94) is not applied. Every other REST endpoint funnels through connect()/authentication.begin(), which enforces this permission (DataServiceController.java:577-584 and its call sites at 103, 161, 237, 303, 442, 462, 488, 551), and login itself refuses to return a session for users without the permission (LoginServiceController.java:146-156). The file endpoints therefore expose a second, weaker authentication path to the same dispatcher servlet.
candidates.title: File upload/download endpoints accept any valid user session and omit the add-on's 'jpawebapi.api.enabled' permission check
candidates.trace: HTTP POST /upload?s=<uuid> -> FileUploadController.upload (76-109) -> getSession (168-184) returns the session if userSessionService.getUserSession(sessionId) does not throw NoUserSessionException, with no permission check -> getFileDescriptor builds a FileDescriptor from attacker-supplied name/ext/size (186-212) -> uploadToMiddleware posts the body to the core /upload endpoint using the same session (111-152) -> saveFileDescriptor commits the FileDescriptor under the session (163-166). HTTP GET /download?s=<uuid>&f=<fileUuid> -> RestFileDownloadController.download (81-125) -> getSession (193-209) with no permission check -> dataService.load(FileDescriptor) under the session (100) -> writeResponse streams the stored file from the middleware using the same session (127-180).
candidates.unverified: Cannot confirm runtime reachability, whether any real deployment grants a valid session to a user denied jpawebapi.api.enabled, whether a middleware /upload call accepts a non-trusted session as-is, or whether the anonymous session is registered. Library behavior (TrustedClientService, UserSessionService, DataService) was not inspected because CUBA/bali sources are not in the snapshot.

coverage_summary: All 55 model-visible files were listed; the 24 Java sources (35 KB-33 KB controllers and converters), all 18 XML/properties configuration files, build.gradle, README and CI config in the assigned source root were read or searched. The P1 relation index covers 54/55 files (1 file absent from the index; index status 'partial', 1318 unresolved calls, no control-flow/data-flow or semantic resolution, Spring annotation matches unverified), so navigation hints were confirmed against source text. No tests exist in the snapshot and no build/test execution was performed. The review focused on the dispatcher servlet/initializer, Authentication, DataServiceController, LoginServiceController, the two file controllers, both converters, ServiceRequest/CommitRequest/InstanceRef, RestServicePermissions, and the Spring/CORS/web.xml/property configuration; coverage of external CUBA, bali, dom4j, Spring and HttpComponents behavior is necessarily absent.
limitations: No runtime verification, dependency inspection, build or test execution was performed; all conclusions are static source reads.

External libraries that decide several candidate outcomes (TrustedClientService, UserSessionService, DataService, EntityLoadInfo, AbstractViewRepository, com.haulmont.bali.util.Dom4j, Spring Security/CORS) are not in the snapshot, so XXE, commit-classification and view-deployment leads remain unverified.

Application-level security configuration (roles, cuba.restServicesConfig service whitelist, cuba.anonymousSessionId registration, jpawebapi.mapping.url overrides, local.app.properties) is not part of the snapshot; impact of the selected candidate depends on such deployment configuration.
One source file (source_files 55 vs indexed 54) was not represented in the P1 index; the omitted file could not be identified from the index metadata.
The relation index provides syntactic candidates only (no control/data flow, no reachability), so unindexed call paths cannot be excluded.

rejected_leads.lead: Credentials transmitted in the URL by the GET /login endpoint (LoginServiceController.java:121-129, @RequestParam "p"; documented in README.md:67)
rejected_leads.reason: Real sensitive-data-in-URL weakness (CWE-598), but it is the documented, intended login mechanism of the add-on, requires no authorization bypass, and its impact (log/referrer leakage) is lower than the missing-gate defect on the file endpoints. Left unselected to keep a single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE when parsing XML request bodies via com.haulmont.bali.util.Dom4j.readDocument (XMLConverter.java:208, 267, 333, 340, 415; /query, /commit, /service with text/xml)
rejected_leads.reason: The entity-resolution hardening of Dom4j.readDocument lives in the external CUBA/bali library, which is not in the snapshot; whether DOCTYPE/external entities are disabled cannot be verified from source here. Unconfirmed lead, not asserted.

rejected_leads.lead: /deployViews lets any REST-enabled user inject view definitions into the global ViewRepository (DataServiceController.java:435-454; AbstractViewRepository.deployViews at 448)
rejected_leads.reason: No admin check is visible, but data exposure/side effects depend on AbstractViewRepository library semantics and on other clients using colliding view names; converters still enforce attribute VIEW permissions and DataService enforces row-level security, so a concrete security impact could not be established from source.

rejected_leads.lead: Service whitelist matches only service+method names while the caller can choose overloads via client-supplied parameter types (RestServicePermissions.isNotPermitted 64-73; ServiceRequest.findMethod 67-93; ClassUtils.forName in DataServiceController.java:518, JSONConverter.java:397, XMLConverter.java:294/396)
rejected_leads.reason: The authorization check is genuinely signature-blind, but the service whitelist (cuba.restServicesConfig, RestServicePermissions.java:48/92) is not present in the snapshot and no concrete dangerous overload was identified, so exploitability is unproven.

rejected_leads.lead: Commit create/update classification is driven by client-declared new instance ids (DataServiceController.commitPermitted 633-645 and isNewInstance 408-419, fed by CommitRequest.parseInstanceRefAndRegister 72-105)
rejected_leads.reason: Whether an existing entity can be mis-declared as new (thus checking CREATE instead of UPDATE) depends on the EntityLoadInfo.isNewEntity()/toString() semantics in the external CUBA library, which is not in the snapshot; cannot be verified.

rejected_leads.lead: CORS configured with allowedOrigins '*' and allowCredentials=true in the dispatcher and app-component defaults (jpawebapi-dispatcher-spring.xml:46-65; app-component.xml:43,59; sample cuba.rest.allowedOrigins="*")
rejected_leads.reason: Authentication uses a URL parameter session id, not cookies, so cross-origin credentialed reads are not directly enabled; browsers/Spring reject or ignore '*' with credentials. No concrete exploit path could be shown.

rejected_leads.lead: Stack traces returned to clients when cuba.rest.productionMode is false, which is the declared default (JpaWebApiConfig.java:36-38; DataServiceController.sendError 593-606)
rejected_leads.reason: Information disclosure only affects error responses of already-authenticated REST calls; configuration-dependent and much lower impact than the selected candidate.

summary: Reviewed the 55-file, 24-Java-file snapshot of the CUBA jpawebapi add-on (REST API over the middleware DataService, login/logout, file upload/download, JSON/XML converters, dispatcher Spring config). Authentication is session-UUID based: DataServiceController and LoginServiceController route every request through Authentication.begin(), which verifies the session via TrustedClientService and enforces the add-on-specific permission 'jpawebapi.api.enabled' (Authentication.java:55, 70-98; DataServiceController.connect 577-584). The single strongest source-supported lead is that the two file controllers do not use that gate at all: they accept any existing session UUID via userSessionService.getUserSession(), so a user explicitly denied the REST API permission (login explicitly rejects such users, LoginServiceController 146-156) can still reach /upload and /download. Entity-level CRUD and row-level checks performed by DataService under the same session still bound the impact, and the session UUID is an unguessable bearer secret, so this is an authorization-consistency defect rather than a proven full compromise. Other plausible issues (XXE on XML request bodies, view redeployment, service-overload whitelist bypass, client-driven new/update classification in the commit check, credentials in the GET login query string) were checked and left as rejected/unconfirmed leads because the deciding behavior lives in external libraries or application configuration not present in this snapshot.
